corroboratingSources.role: Whole-zero maximum, explicit non-damaging spells, positive Sunfire minimum and rounded-zero multihit eligibility.
Successful magic damage uses the same zero conversion.

implementationScope: Shared player melee/ranged/powered-staff/spell sampling, with an explicit positive-whole-attack eligibility seam for split hits. Accuracy, maximum formulas, NPC sampling and downstream modifiers are unchanged.
testBoundary: Real PlayerAttackManager, native cache entities and standard target hit modifiers; maximum/accuracy formula dependencies are controlled to enumerate sampling outcomes. Existing MagicSplashHitTest covers queued impact and HP-floor/cap behavior.
limits: Whole-max-zero and rounded-zero-subhit exceptions are corroborated by the pinned current calculator; no exhaustive primary Jagex statement for all unusual equipment/stat configurations was located.
This does not certify weapon-specific damage transformations, claw specials, proc timing, PvP damage-reduction ordering or every hit distribution.

pvpElysianMigration.scope: PvP maximum helpers return raw maxima without Elysian RNG. Ordinary typed player-attack queues explicitly opt into one shield proc per positive hit. Legacy direct/deferred/instant and unrelated player-sourced hits remain opt-out.
pvpElysianMigration.preservedPolicy: Existing collectPvP eligibility is Elysian only (7 of10 proc slots); damage uses floor(3*sampledDamage/4), before existing PvP protection-prayer reduction. This preserves previous rounding and ordering policy, not a new full live-OSRS rounding/order certification.
exclusions: No Dinh, Justiciar or Ward PvP mitigation is added.

The existing caller contract computes combat XP before queuing damage and is unchanged. With raw maxima, XP now sees pre-Elysian sampled damage rather than the former Elysian-reduced maximum; exact live PvP XP behavior and shield/prayer order remain unverified. PvP hook inputs remain pre-mitigation; the Wilderness hook ignores amount and Corruption uses it as a successful-hit proxy.
